references.text: Moses asks God to blot him out of His book if the people are not forgiven. This illustrates the concept of writing and blotting out in a book, similar to how the priest writes the curses and then washes them away in water.
The psalmist prays that enemies be blotted out from the book of life. The idea of erasing something written parallels the priest's action in Numbers 5:23.
The Lord will wash away the uncleanness of the daughters of Zion. Washing and cleansing with water is thematically connected to the bitter water used in the ritual of purification.
Earlier in the same chapter, the bitter water that brings a curse is described. Verse 23 explains how the curses are transferred to the water through writing and washing out.
The next verse states that the woman shall drink the bitter water. This shows the continuation of the ritual where the written curses are now in the water.
Jesus promises that whoever overcomes will not have their name blotted out from the book of life. The concept of writing and blotting names from a book is thematically related.
